verdict.rationale: GitLab's Duo Agent Platform lets users build custom flows that automate team processes. Users define workflow steps, agents, and triggers that control when a flow runs, and sessions report the status of runs. This is a direct, first-party capability for setting up automations that run without manual prompting. However, the evidence is short marketing and doc snippets: it never shows unattended background or recurring scheduled execution, and nothing independent corroborates it. missing for 10: explicit documentation of background or scheduled execution of flows without a human present, detail on trigger types and their depth, independent or hands-on corroboration that autonomous runs work as claimed.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Custom flows are workflows you create to automate your team’s specific processes.
You define the workflow steps and agents, and define triggers to control when the flow runs.
Delegate routine tasks, from code refactoring and security scans to research, to specialized AI agents.
Sessions show the status and execution data for the agents and flows you’ve run.
